chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Footnote on Avis Andrews and Cab Calloway
summary: Hughes adds that photos show Avis Andrews, who sang with Cab Calloway and in the Harold Arlen show 'Great Day'.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Okay. I guess what we're going to say now is something in the way of a footnote referring back to our last topics of conversation when we had Chester Campbell, Jr., here, giving some of his reminiscences about his father and you were also talking about Cliff Jackson and we were doing a little bit of research and we found some of the photos that were being referred to in those conversations. There's a photograph of Cliff Jackson's Krazy Kats in which Chester Campbell also appears. And Albert McCarthy's book, "Big Band Jazz." And we've also been looking in Stanley Dance's book, "The World of Earl Hines," and let me see, on page 24 of that book, for instance, there's a list the black AFM Local, it's Local No. 471 in Pittsburgh. It's a list of names and we see Chester Campbell listed there along with your uncle, Harry Williams and numerous other people we'll come to talk about in a little while. And also several pictures in that book of Hedy Stath one with Harry
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Williams in the photo and another one taken in 1929, Atlantic City, which has Avis Andrews who's someone you've mentioned on this tape a long way back, too.

Well, yes, I got to know Avis Andrews naturally after I came to New York but I think I mentioned earlier that on an occasion when I was supposed to appear at the Apollo Theater and they had the bill as John Kirby and Maxine Sullivan, I didn't show up for that engagement and Avis Andrews sat in -- in fact she fulfilled the engagement that week because I had spoken to Shiffman earlier stating that I didn't want to appear on the bill at the same time with John Kirby when he hadn't booked it anyway.
It also mentions that she sang with Cab Calloway.

Yes, well, I wouldn't have known about that. She was quite popular at the time and of course in that particular picture in 1929, that was a scene of the cast from the movie that Lois Deppe appeared in so she must have been among the singers in that group.

Well, it was a show on the road anyway, Harold Arlen show, "Great Day."
